board.name: Source class
board.requirement: Every input field resolves to an official NBA page or the official injury PDF.
board.measured: 14 declared sources, all on nba.com, ak-static.cms.nba.com or another official host

board.name: Completeness
board.requirement: No required input is blank. A blank anywhere fails the strategy for that slate.
board.measured: 8/34 slate games have an official availability record for both clubs; 26 do not (dates beyond the newest injury release)

board.name: Sample floor
board.requirement: >= 10 official games observed by BOTH teams before a line may be graded above C.
board.measured: league-wide minimum games behind a team rating: 11 (DEN); the per-line bar is applied in model.originated_lines

board.name: Estimator agreement
board.requirement: Two independent ratings (net points/game; NetRtg) must imply spreads within 2.0 pts.

board.name: Total-estimator agreement
board.measured: largest gap across the 34-game slate: 4.56 pts (threshold 6.00)
board.requirement: PF/PA total and per-100x-pace total must be within 4.0 pts.

board.name: Market price present
board.requirement: A dated, sourced price for the exact line must exist before a pick is staked.
board.measured: no odds snapshot in data/raw; no licensed feed is connected, so no edge, stake, ROI or CLV claim is available for any game — 0/34 slate games carry a price

board.name: Backtest with settlement
board.requirement: >= 300 settled bets of the strategy's own signals, settled from official box scores.

board.name: Out-of-sample holdout
board.measured: in-sample 63.4% vs out-of-sample 67.3% (+/- 7.1% s.e.); MAE 12.22 -> 13.23. The signal holds out of sample.
board.requirement: Signals fitted on the first 70% of the backtest window must hold on the last 30%.

board.name: Luck screen
board.requirement: Every team the strategy relies on must be inside the luck noise band (|z| <= 1.96).

board.name: Correlation honesty
board.requirement: No parlay priced by multiplying legs unless the leg correlation is measured or bounded.

capture.method: platform page-fetch tool (fetch_page). Direct TLS egress from this workspace to every nba.com host is blocked; the tool reaches the same URLs, which is recorded rather than worked around. Each document below carries the URL it was read from.
identities_passed: 5/5 games: quarter scores sum to the final score on both sides, read independently from the game page and from the game book, and the two documents agree
30/30 standings rows: home + road + neutral games = games played; wins and losses split by venue; every conference and division figure inside the season record
30/30 CONF columns equal the intra-conference record computed game by game from the 188-game result feed
league wins = league losses = 188 = twice the number of games
30/30 records rebuilt from the per-game result feed equal the standings card
30/30 games-played agreement across four documents: the standings card, the advanced page, the opponent page and the traditional page
30/30 W-L agreement between the standings card, the advanced page and the traditional page
30/30 NetRtg within a tenth of OffRtg - DefRtg (each printed to 0.1)
30/30 opponent-page points allowed x GP equals points-allowed rebuilt from the finals
30/30 advanced-page OffRtg x POSS/100 equals points-for rebuilt from the finals

30/30 traditional-page points x GP equals points-for rebuilt from the finals; OREB + DREB = REB; the implied OffRtg is within 0.35 of the printed one; pts - opponent pts equals the margin rebuilt from the finals
the LAST 10 column sums to exactly 300 team-games (30 teams x 10)

the OT column implies exactly the 10 overtime games in the feed, and the Neutral column the one neutral-site game — which is how the five 11/14 games are known not to have gone to overtime or been played at a neutral site
per-date game counts match the official day-strip calendar: 9 games on 11/15, 8 on 11/16, 5 on 11/17
the injury report's own game grid matches nba.com/schedule for 11/15 (9 games) and 11/16 (8 games), and every printed 12-hour tip time converts to the schedule's ET time
the two injury releases differ in exactly one row and one field: a surname spelling
84 designation rows per release, every row inside the 11/15 game date, every team a club in its own matchup, and rows in the PDF's alphabetical order inside each team block
no game-book team shooting line passed 2 x FGM + FTM = points: all six were discarded and flagged rather than published
named leader lines never exceed the team's final score in any of the 10 clubs

injury_release_diff.method: row-for-row comparison of the two releases, keyed on the normalised player string so the spelling variant does not read as a status change

spelling_only.reason: Injury/Illness - Right Foot Plantar Fascia Injury Management

injury_release_diff.consequence: no line on the 11/15 slate can move between the day's two releases; the model's availability input for 11/15 was already final at 06:15 ET

what_the_harness_does_not_prove: The identities prove internal and cross-document consistency, not the fidelity of a single printed cell: changing a status from Out to Probable would pass every check. The control on that is that both releases were read twice, independently, in this session, and agreed row for row.

The 188-game result feed is only as good as the committed history snapshots it is built from; those came from earlier sessions' reads of nba.com/games and are not re-verified here game by game, only in aggregate (they reproduce today's standings card exactly, including every conference record, which no single wrong score could survive).
Player-level lines are context. Nothing in this capture uses a game-book player row as a model input, because the PDF text layer misaligns columns.
notes: Consecutive official releases, fifteen minutes apart (06:00 AM and 06:15 AM ET on 2026-11-15), are identical in content: same 84 designation rows, same single Dallas non-submission, same 16-slot 11/16 non-submission block. The only textual difference is the spelling of the Philadelphia centre's surname — "Embiid, Joel" at 06:00, "Embid, Joel" at 06:15, same team, status and reason. Both spellings are kept verbatim in the two snapshots; matching is done on a normalised player key so the typo does not surface as a phantom status change.

The PDF prints tip times on a 12-hour clock with an "(ET)" suffix. All nine 11/15 game times and all eight 11/16 game times in the PDF match nba.com/schedule exactly (01:00 = 1:00 PM ET, 04:00 = 4:00 PM ET, 07:30 = 7:30 PM ET, and so on).

Dallas is the only club that had not filed for a 2026-11-15 game in either release: DAL@BOS prints "NOT YET SUBMITTED" against the Mavericks and nothing against them at any later hour. For the eight 2026-11-16 games, all 16 club-slots print "NOT YET SUBMITTED", and 2026-11-17 does not appear in the document at all.

New York filed no designation rows for its 11/15 game and no non-submission marker either. That is read as a clean filing — an empty report — rather than a missing document. The reading is an interpretation and is labelled as one on the site.

Six 11/15 rows are continuation rows: the PDF broke a page mid-block, so the game date, matchup and team cells are blank on the printed line. The team is carried over from the block and every one of those rows is marked "C" (carried) in the snapshot. Sacramento's Ben Simmons row is the extreme case — all four leading cells, including the team cell, are empty; it is attached to Sacramento by block position and flagged, never asserted.

Denver's 11/14 game book lists the Pelicans' Dejounte Murray as inactive with a left ankle sprain, and the recap on the same page records that he requested a trade on Friday. A roster-mover fact has no input in this model (R-106) and is published as a note only.

Cleveland's game book lists seven inactive players — five of a usual starting five — plus two more (Allen, Watson) marked DND, did not dress, after the day's last injury release. A game-day change of that size is invisible to any model fed only by the morning report, which is why availability is scored against the game book and not the PDF alone.

The 11/14 game books also carry two source-side defects that are published rather than quietly repaired: James Harden's inactive line reads "Right Elbow Injury Management" while the recap on the same page attributes his absence to a left calf, and one Detroit period strip in the DET@MIA book prints "20 21 26 21 117", which cannot be a quarter line. Both are flagged; neither is used.

still_blocked.what: Per-player season game logs (minutes by game, for players who did not play)
still_blocked.attempted: nba.com/stats/player/<id>/gamelog renders client-side and returns 'No data available' to this client; the same failure was reported by session arena/bc867bff-nba2 on 2026-11-14.
still_blocked.consequence: Minutes redistribution is modelled from the official game books of the games a player missed — who actually played and how many minutes they took — so coverage is 2026-11-14 (10 clubs), not the season. Any line that would depend on a bench player's season-long usage is left unpriced.
